findings.title: Shard-split queries are interpolated multiple times
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates every target here, but splitQueriesByStreamShard (line 163) then passes those targets to runSplitQuery, which at querySplitting.ts:299 calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables again for every shard/time sub-request; the updated shard test even expects 5 applyTemplateVariables calls for one original query. Loki's applyTemplateVariables also injects request.filters adhoc filters into the stream selector and re-runs template replacement, neither of which is guaranteed idempotent: repeated passes can add the same adhoc matcher again and can re-expand $-sequences introduced by a first-pass variable value, besides re-parsing already-interpolated LogQL per chunk. Interpolation should be owned by one layer, e.g. the shard layer should be able to tell runSplitQuery its targets are already interpolated.

findings.title: Split queries are interpolated again by datasource.runQuery for every chunk
findings.body: The queries interpolated here are built into grouped sub-requests and executed via datasource.runQuery in runSplitGroupedQueries (line 180). Loki's runQuery backend path (DataSourceWithBackend.query) applies applyTemplateVariables again with the same scopedVars and request.filters before sending each chunk to the backend, so every split query is now interpolated at least twice, and three times on the shard path. As with the shard double-interpolation, the repeated adhoc-filter injection from request.filters and repeated templateSrv replacement of already-substituted values are not guaranteed idempotent and can corrupt or invalidly duplicate stream-selector matchers. The early interpolation for splitting decisions needs to be reconciled with the downstream one, rather than simply adding another pass.

findings.title: Queries that interpolate to empty are no longer filtered out before sharding
findings.body: The order was changed from interpolate-then-filter to filter-then-interpolate: lines 49-52 test the pre-interpolation expr, so a target such as '$SELECTOR' that resolves to an empty string was previously dropped but now survives into groupTargetsByQueryType, requestSupportsSharding/getSelectorForShardValues and fetchLabelValues with an empty stream selector. It is only dropped later by runSplitQuery's own pre-interpolation filter, which can leave that call with no grouped requests instead of the query simply being ignored as an empty query. Add a post-interpolation expr filter (and apply the same filter-after-interpolate ordering in runSplitQuery).
